_purpose: One permanent, growing entry per bug ever found and fixed via the review process (see conversation log / bug checklist). Unlike the stratified sample in sample_review.py, these are not redrawn each round — they are the same fixed assertions every time, so 'did this specific bug come back' has a yes/no answer instead of depending on which random nodes got sampled this run. Every entry must include enough `locate` fields to resolve to exactly one node (or, for `kind: count`, a deliberately-multi-match set) — evaluate.py treats 0 matches or an unexpected >1 matches as its own AMBIGUOUS/NOT_FOUND status, distinct from PASS/FAIL, precisely so a badly-scoped locate can never silently validate against the wrong node.
_maintenance_rule: When a new bug is found and fixed, add ONE new entry here before moving on. This list should only ever grow. If a deliberate future redesign makes an old entry obsolete, remove it explicitly with a note in the commit/PR — never let an entry silently start failing without a decision about why.

Round D, the most serious bug found: two blocks 0.1pt apart (504.5 vs 504.6) landed in different integer buckets under Python's banker's-rounding `round(top, 0)`, flipping clause 72's heading and its own subclause 72.1's body out of reading order. This misparented 72.1 under the WRONG clause and glued its real text onto clause 72's title fragment instead, producing a fluent but factually wrong sentence with no visible sign of breakage. Fixed with a coarser, tie-safe row bucket (6pt, well under this document's line height).
Companion check to bug_022: 72.2 must also be present and correctly parented, in case a future fix to the tie-break only handles the first sibling.

Round E: `decimal_plain` numbering ("1.", "2.", ...) was classified as node_type='clause' unconditionally, which is only correct for genuine SSUK two-column clause headings. Ordinary flat numbered lists elsewhere (Tembusan lists on p.5, SPMK/SPPBJ instructions on p.6, the PAKTA specimen forms' checklists on p.70-71) got the same 'clause' treatment, which meant the title/text_raw dedup logic (bug_021's fix) wrongly emptied their entire content into `title` and left text_raw blank — real content silently missing from the searchable field. Fixed by classifying decimal_plain as 'clause' only on genuine SSUK-body pages (612x792, identified by page height, not by that specific page's own layout_type — a real SSUK clause can land on a page the two-column detector calls single_column when it's pure body continuation with no heading of its own on that page; verified against clauses 32, 34, 78). This check asserts the total clause-type node count equals exactly the SSUK body's own clause count (80) with zero leaking into any other sub_document.

Not a bug fix — pins an investigated behavior. `NodeIdGenerator` (schema.py) assigns node_id as a plain sequential counter (n_0001, n_0002, ...) in tree-build order, not derived from content. Verified across 3 independent full-pipeline runs on this PDF: every node_id was byte-identical run to run, because every stage feeding the tree sorts explicitly by geometry (word top/x0, block row-bucket/column/x0) before consuming — no dict/set iteration order, threading, or randomness anywhere in the path. So node_id IS stable for a fixed (code, input) pair. It is NOT a durable identity: it is positional, so inserting/deleting any node upstream (e.g. a future bug fix that changes how many blocks a page produces) shifts every subsequent node_id even though those nodes' own content didn't change — this is why retrieval/'s embedding-view keys are derived from hierarchy_path+label_normalized instead of raw node_id. This check exists to catch the OTHER failure mode: a future edit that introduces real nondeterminism (e.g. a set() iterated instead of a sorted list) in the tree-build path, which would make node_id vary between runs on the SAME input.

Companion to node_id_stable_first_node, deep in the tree rather than at the root — a nondeterminism bug introduced late in tree-build order could leave the first few node_ids stable by luck while everything after them drifts. Pins clause 72's node_id (same node bug_022's checks already locate by content).
